To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

relationship specific investments encourage suppliers to share ideas of process innovations with customers, that this effect is stronger when the supplier is more experienced in the relationship and when the relationship is long term, and that this effect is weaker when the supplier is less experienced and when the relationship lacks safeguards.

(i) relationship specific investments by suppliers encourage them to share innovative ideas with their customers; (ii) this positive relationship is stronger in the context of process innovations than in the context of product innovations; and (iii) the relationship between relationship specific investments by a supplier and its sharing of innovative product ideas with a customer can be weakened by the presence of formal and informal safeguards in the customer supplier relationship.

a buyer should not only be concerned with the level of relationship specific investments but should also be aware of the specific type of investments.

relationship specific investments are a double edged sword for supplier innovation sharing: they encourage the supplier to suggest process innovation ideas but they discourage the supplier to suggest product innovation ideas.
